title: Fix Pinata directory upload 400 error: "More than one file and/or directory was provided for pinning."

requirements.text: Update the Pinata directory upload implementation so uploading a generated collection to Pinata no longer fails with HTTP 400: {"error":"More than one file and/or directory was provided for pinning."}. This includes adjusting the multipart/form-data payload sent to https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/pinFileToIPFS to match Pinata’s directory upload expectations when multiple files are provided (and the request must still use JWT Bearer auth).

quotes: Still get this error "Upload failed: Directory upload failed: 400 - {"error":"More than one file and/or directory was provided for pinning."}"
1. Yes pls check carefully and update the Pinata upload code again to try to fix this error

acceptanceCriteria: From the Vault publishing flow, uploading a typical full generated collection (images + metadata) completes successfully and returns a directory CID for images and a CID for the metadata JSON.
The request remains a POST to https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/pinFileToIPFS with Authorization: Bearer <JWT> (no endpoint or auth mechanism changes).
If the directory upload still fails for any reason, the UI error message includes both the HTTP status code and the response body text (when available), preserving the existing diagnostics behavior.

requirements.text: Ensure the image URI paths in generated metadata remain correct after the directory-upload payload change (e.g., if files are uploaded under a directory prefix/path, metadata must reference ipfs://<imageDirCID>/<correct relative path>).

acceptanceCriteria: After a successful upload, at least one sampled token’s metadata image field resolves to an existing file under the returned images directory CID using the expected token filename convention (e.g., 0.png / 1.png depending on settings).
No regressions to existing token numbering behavior (startTokenNumberAtZero continues to affect filenames/URIs consistently).

constraints: Frontend files under frontend.immutablePaths must not be edited.
Keep the Pinata upload endpoint as https://api.pinata.cloud/pinning/pinFileToIPFS and continue using JWT Bearer authorization.
Do not introduce external backend services or databases; keep all changes within the existing React/TS frontend utilities and components.
nonGoals: Adding new chains/metadata formats (Polygon/Base/BNB, default chain changes, removal of Cardano/Tezos).
Implementing ICP-native storage or any new backend-based IPFS pinning flow.
Changing the lock/unlock publishing UX beyond what is necessary to surface correct upload results/errors.
